bandierina.ricorrenza: Desfile de Faroles and the arrival of the Independence Torch
bandierina.dialogo:
ARDE: This, Filippo, is the flag of Costa Rica — five bold stripes, blue, white, and red, and a coat of arms full of stories!

FILIPPO: Beautiful! And tonight, all across Costa Rica, those colors will be glowing in the streets, because it's the night of the Desfile de Faroles!

ARDE: Exactly — the Parade of Lanterns! Children and families march through every town carrying hand-made paper lanterns, celebrating the eve of Independence Day on September 15th.

FILIPPO: And what about the famous Independence Torch? That seems like something with a real history behind it!

ARDE: Oh, it's a wonderful tradition! Since 1964, a symbolic flame is lit in Guatemala City — where Central America's independence was first declared in 1821 — and relay runners carry it all the way south to Costa Rica in time for the celebrations.

FILIPPO: Incredible! Now, Professor, show us where Costa Rica sits on the map!

ARDE: Here we are — Costa Rica is the jewel of Central America, nestled between Nicaragua to the north and Panama to the south, with the Pacific Ocean on one side and the Caribbean Sea on the other. Tiny in size, enormous in spirit!

FILIPPO: Perfect — and now, let's see if our audience has been paying attention... it's time for the domandone!

dialogo.testo: This, Filippo, is the flag of Costa Rica — five bold stripes, blue, white, and red, and a coat of arms full of stories!
Wonderful! And right now, all across the country, families are lighting up their lanterns for the Desfile de Faroles — the magical Parade of Lanterns on the eve of Independence Day!
And when we say 'all across the country,' we really mean it — Costa Rica is divided into 82 cantones, its municipalities, and every single one of them celebrates with their own local parade!
82 cantones! That's a lot of lanterns glowing in the dark. But Professor, how big is Costa Rica exactly? Is it easy to imagine 82 municipalities fitting inside it?

Surprisingly compact! Costa Rica covers just about 51,000 square kilometers — smaller than the Italian region of Lombardy and Veneto combined — yet it holds about 6% of the world's entire biodiversity. Tiny but extraordinary!
Extraordinary indeed! Now, Professor, can you show us exactly where this little wonder sits on the map?

With pleasure! Here it is — right in the heart of Central America, hugged by Nicaragua to the north and Panama to the south, with the Pacific on the west and the Caribbean on the east. A true crossroads of nature and culture!
What a location! Alright folks, keep those lanterns in mind — because it's time for the domandone!

ospiteRef.bio: Luca Bruschi is the director of AEVF, European Association of the Via Francigena Ways. As Director, Bruschi is at the forefront of the nomination of the Via Francigena as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In July, the preliminary dossier was officially submitted in Paris, focusing on the Italian section of the route from the Great St. Bernard Pass to Rome. The next stage of the candidacy will begin at the end of September 2025: this phase involves compiling the final dossier, identifying the cultural assets to be included on the UNESCO list, producing detailed cartography, and organizing participatory meetings with local communities along the route.The Via Francigena is certified Cultural Route of the Council of Europe. More than 3000 kilometers, from Canterbury to Rome and Santa Maria di Leuca, to walk step by step on mountain paths, mule tracks, rural and secondary roads, cypress-lined dirt roads or among majestic pines. Bruschi has personally completed the Via Francigena, the Camino de Santiago, and many other pilgrimage routes and cultural itineraries across Europe.

script.dialogo:
FILIPPO: Roma gets dressed up for the arts — the Romaeuropa Festival is back, running from September 8th all the way to November 15th, spreading across 20 venues in the Eternal City. Contemporary creation, international stages, and that very Roman mix of chaos and genius.

ARDE: Exactly, Filippo — 20 spaces, 68 days of programming, and this is the 41st edition, which they're calling RE41F. That's four decades of bringing the world's avant-garde to a city where the Colosseum is basically the warm-up act.

FILIPPO: Forty-one years of this festival means it started in 1985 — when shoulder pads were a personality and contemporary dance was considered dangerous. Rome has changed. The shoulder pads, thankfully, less so.

ARDE: And if you do the math, 20 venues across 68 days means Rome is essentially one giant theatre for over two months. My solution? Move in. Sublet your apartment and live in a different venue each week — culturally optimal, financially terrifying.

FILIPPO: Trending number two!

FILIPPO: Alright, we're talking about the Festival del Parco di Monza — one of Italy's most beloved green events, set inside the historic Monza Park, right at Via Alessandro Pennati 10. A summer gathering that brings together music, nature, and culture in one of Europe's largest walled parks.

ARDE: And Filippo, that park is no small thing — the Parco di Monza covers approximately 688 hectares, making it one of the largest enclosed parks on the entire continent. That's a lot of grass to festival on.

FILIPPO: 688 hectares of festival vibes — honestly, you could get lost in there and still have a great time. It's the kind of event that reminds Italians living abroad exactly why they miss home in June.

ARDE: Precisely. And if attendance follows typical Italian outdoor festival patterns, you're looking at tens of thousands of visitors over multiple days — though I would suggest organisers install GPS chips in all attendees, given those 688 hectares.

FILIPPO: GPS chips, Arde. Right. For the record, that is not official festival policy. Trending number two!

bandierina.ricorrenza: Slovakia: Day of Our Lady of Sorrows

direzioni.descrizione: Direzione A – focus storico: le origini medievali della devozione mariana in Slovacchia e il legame con l'identità nazionale
direzioni.domandone_sintesi: Curiosità geografica: quale catena montuosa simbolo della Slovacchia è visibile anche nel suo stemma nazionale?

dialogo.testo: This, Filippo, is the flag of Slovakia! White, blue and red — classic Pan-Slavic colours, with a very special coat of arms right in the middle.
A double cross on three hills — it looks almost like a medieval emblem. Very proud, very dignified!

Exactly! And today Slovakia celebrates the Day of Our Lady of Sorrows — the Feast of the Seven Sorrows of the Virgin Mary — which is actually the country's national holiday as well as a religious feast.
A national holiday AND a religious feast? So Slovaks have a very deep bond between their faith and their national identity?

Absolutely. This devotion goes back centuries — it flourished here in the Middle Ages and became so rooted in Slovak culture that when modern Slovakia was defining itself, Our Lady of Sorrows was chosen as the country's heavenly patron. Faith and nation, intertwined since the very beginning.
Wonderful! Now, Professor, show us where Slovakia actually is on the map!

Here we are — right in the heart of Central Europe! Slovakia borders Poland to the north, Ukraine to the east, Hungary to the south, and Austria and the Czech Republic to the west. Bratislava, the capital, sits almost on the Austrian border — just an hour's drive from Vienna!
A true crossroads of Europe! Alright everyone, stay with us — it's time for the domandone!

dialogo.testo: This, Filippo, is the flag of Slovakia! White, blue and red — classic Pan-Slavic colours, with a very special coat of arms right in the middle.
A double cross on three hills — it looks almost like a medieval emblem. Very proud, very dignified!
Today Slovakia celebrates the Day of Our Lady of Sorrows — their national patron — and it is also the country's official national holiday. A beautiful blend of spirituality and national pride!
I love that a country chooses a feast of compassion and reflection as its national day. There's something very poetic about that.

Very poetic indeed! And Slovakia itself is full of surprises. Did you know it holds a rather extraordinary European record? Its capital Bratislava is the only capital city in the world that borders TWO other sovereign countries — Austria and Hungary — at the same time!
No! A capital city with two international borders? That is genuinely remarkable. Professor, show us on the map!

Here it is — smack in the southwest corner of the country! Bratislava hugs the Danube river, with Austria literally a few kilometres to the west and Hungary just across the river to the south. Vienna is closer to Bratislava than many Slovak cities are. It's one of the most fascinating geographical situations in all of Europe!
A capital at the edge of the world — or rather, at the crossroads of three worlds! Alright everyone, stay with us — it's time for the domandone!

script.dialogo:
FILIPPO: It's that time of year on the Italian Alps — the rut is in full swing, and the red deer are out there doing their very loud, very dramatic thing. The bramito, that deep roaring call of the male deer, is echoing through the mountains right now.

ARDE: Filippo, the roar of a red deer stag can be heard from up to 2 kilometres away. Two kilometres. That is more effective than most Italian mobile phone networks in the mountains.

FILIPPO: And yet somehow my signal drops the moment I enter a tunnel on the A1. The stags have us beat. But tell me — is this a rare sight, or are the deer actually thriving up there?

ARDE: The red deer population in the Alpine arc has grown significantly over recent decades, which is wonderful for romantically inclined ungulates and slightly less wonderful for farmers near the treeline. My proposed solution: send the deer to Rai meetings. The roaring would save at least 40 minutes per session.

FILIPPO: I would absolutely vote for that. Alright, if you are somewhere in the Alps this autumn, keep your ears open — that sound is one of the great spectacles of Italian nature. Trending number two!

calEvents.title: Self-injury Awareness Day
calEvents.note:
Self-injury Awareness Day (SIAD) is a grassroots annual global awareness event / campaign on March 1, where on this day, and in the weeks leading up to it and after, some people choose to be more open about their own self-harm, and awareness organizations make special efforts to raise awareness about self-harm and self-injury. Some people wear an orange awareness ribbon, write "LOVE" on their arms, draw a butterfly on their wrists in awareness of "the Butterfly Project" wristband or beaded bracelet to encourage awareness of self-harm. The goal of the people who observe SIAD is to break down the common stereotypes surrounding self-harm and to educate medical professionals about the condition.

World Day Against Cyber Censorship
calEvents.note:
Basato sull'evento 18 anni fa (2008).

World Day Against Cyber Censorship is an online event held each year on March 12 to rally support for a single, unrestricted Internet that is accessible to all and to draw attention to the ways that governments around the world are deterring and censoring free speech online. The day was first observed on 12 March 2008 at the request of Reporters Without Borders and Amnesty International. A letter written by Jean-François Julliard, Secretary-General of Reporters Without Borders, and Larry Cox, Executive Director of Amnesty International, was sent to the Chief Executive Officers of Google, Yahoo!, Inc., and Microsoft Corporation to request observation of the day.
The annual event is symbolized by a logo created by Reporters Without Borders consisting of a computer mouse breaking free from a chain.

International No Diet Day (INDD) is an annual celebration of body acceptance, including fat acceptance and body shape diversity. The first International No Diet Day was celebrated in the UK in 1992. Feminist groups in other countries around the globe have started to celebrate International No Diet Day, especially in the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India, Israel, Denmark, Sweden and Brazil.

calEvents.title: 🌬️ Global Wind Day
calEvents.note:
Basato sull'evento 274 anni fa (1752).

Global Wind Day or World Wind Day is a worldwide event that is held on June 15 around the world. It is organised by WindEurope and GWEC .
 It is a day when wind energy is celebrated, information is exchanged and adults and children find out about wind energy, its power and the possibilities it holds to change the world. 
In association with EWEA and GWEC, national wind energy associations and companies involved in wind energy production organise events in many countries around the world. In 2011, there were events organised in 30 countries, on 4 continents. Events included visits to onshore and offshore wind farms, information campaigns, demonstration turbines being set up in cities, wind workshops and a wind parade. Many events happened on Global Wind Day itself, but there were also events on the days and weeks before and afterwards. In 2012 there were 250 events around the globe and a very popular photo competition.

A Cagli il fungo cambia stagione, nome e profumo. Dallo spignolo alle specie che si alternano grazie al microclima appenninico, l’evento invita a scoprire boschi, sapori, saperi micologici e cucina di montagna.
calEvents.title: Cagli Tutto Fungo
EVO - I Linguaggi del gioco
calEvents.note: EVO a Macerata esplora i linguaggi del gioco tra videogame, giochi da tavolo, social, storytelling, cibo, città e relazioni. Un’esperienza diffusa per leggere il presente giocando sul serio.

La Festa del Torrone chiude a Camerino il periodo natalizio nel giorno dell’Epifania. Tra storia ducale, tradizione camerte e grande taglio del maxi torrone, il dolce simbolo della città diventa rito collettivo.
calEvents.title: XXV Festa del Torrone

calEvents.note: La Festa della Cicerchia accende Serra de’ Conti con fuochi, taverne, profumi e voci. Il legume antico del borgo diventa protagonista di piatti semplici e sorprendenti, tra vicoli, cantine e spazi storici.
calEvents.title: La Festa della Cicerchia

calEvents.note: Appassimenti Aperti apre a Serrapetrona i luoghi dove la Vernaccia Nera riposa sospesa. Cantine, degustazioni e racconti dei produttori svelano le due anime del territorio: Vernaccia DOCG e Serrapetrona DOC.
calEvents.title: Appassimenti Aperti
Sibillini in Rosa
calEvents.note: Sibillini in Rosa celebra a Montedinove la Mela Rosa dei Monti Sibillini, frutto antico, profumato e resistente. Tra sapori, mercatini, laboratori e racconti, la biodiversità diventa una festa gentile e incantata.

Leguminaria mette in tavola ad Appignano legumi antichi, biodiversità locale e cocci di ceramica fatti a mano. Cece Quercia, fagiolo Solfì e sapori di casa raccontano terra, artigianato e convivialità.
calEvents.title: Leguminaria
Sagra de li Sughitti
calEvents.note: La Sagra de li sughitti celebra a Montecassiano un dolce contadino De.Co. a base di mosto, farina di mais e noci. Naturalmente gluten free, vegan e senza zuccheri aggiunti, è una festa d’autunno profumata di vendemmia.

Daniele Grassucci
An aeronautical engineer who has made a name for himself as a journalist and start-up entrepreneur. A true “nerd,” he continues to help millions of students through Skuola.net, which he founded in high school with his classmate Marco Sbardella. For years, he has been following everything related to education and youth lifestyles, constantly appearing as an expert on radio, in newspapers, and on television.

guests.bio: Director of Scientific Laboratories at the Centro per la Conservazione ed il Restauro dei Beni Culturali “La Venaria Reale”, one of the strategic poles for the training, study, and research on cultural heritage in Italy. Prior to my current appointment, I also held positions at several museums and universities in the United States, including The Metropolitan Museum of Art, the City College of the City University of New York, The Art Institute of Chicago, and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. While having performed extensive research with Raman and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) for the identification of pigments and colorants in objects of archaeological, historical, and artistic significance, I gained broad experience with numerous analytical techniques and cultural heritage materials.

guests.bio: RICCARDO ALBINI Journalist and creator of Fantacalcio, which was ideated after a Nafl Fantasy Football guide he stumble upon during the eighties. He was the founder of the first italian videogames magazine, Videogiochi, and found the guide at Consumer Electronic Show in Chicago. He developed the game's rules with some friends and played the first tournament during Euro 1988. He published a book explaining the game in 1990 and in 1994 he made an agreement with Gazzetta dello Sport for the first national tournament: 70k fantasy coaches subscribed to the game.It is estimated that nowadays around 5-6 million people play Fantacalcio in Italy, This number is constantly growing and Fantacalcio is considered a real mass phenomenon involving even more enthusiasts than those who play football at an amateur level. guests.bio: Fabio Testi is the star who turned his good looks from a supposed “flaw” into a ticket to cinematic legend. Born in Peschiera del Garda, he started out as a stuntman — falling off horses, crashing motorbikes, and even hanging in midair for two weeks on the set of Barbarella. It was Vittorio De Sica who catapulted him to fame with the Oscar-winning The Garden of the Finzi-Continis in 1970. From there came a career packed with auteur films and popular hits (Addio fratello crudele, L’important c’est d’aimer with Romy Schneider, Camorra by Pasquale Squitieri), over a hundred screen and stage credits, and a love life straight out of the tabloids — Ursula Andress, Anita Ekberg, Charlotte Rampling, Edwige Fenech… Today, well into his eighties, Testi still keeps us guessing: he grows truffles by Lake Garda, tours with a poetry-and-music show, and pops up in international cinema — most recently in Reflet dans un diamant mort, which premiered at the Berlinale. Always elegant, always magnetic, he’s living proof that yes, there really are a few beautiful men who are also smart.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Professor SERGIO STEFANNI: Born in Desenzano del Garda (Italy) on 29/12/1967, after a Master Degree in marine studies at University of Genoa and a PhD at the School of Biological Science at the University of Bristol, he has been a researcher at Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn in Naples (Italy) since 2016. His research interests are molecular ecology, population genetics and phylogeny of marine organisms. He study mainly fish and sharks, from coastal to the deep-sea, but he's been a guest of Paparazzi helping our understanding of marine alien species in our seas like the lionfish and the silver-cheeked toadfish. ANDREA LEVY: Andrea Levy was born in Ancona on July 7, 1971. He specialized in international marketing and communication at the University of Nevada. His passion for cars has been with him since childhood. He grew up in Moncalieri, near Turin, where he saw prototypes and cars from legendary coachbuilders and manufacturers—Pininfarina, Giugiaro, Italdesign, and Fiat—come to life and hit the roads. Today, he is a successful entrepreneur in communication and events, a devoted collector of sports cars and supercars, and a true motorsport enthusiast. He races with Ferrari Club Italia and competes in Time Attack with Ferrari, Radical, and Dallara. Always on the move, he follows racing competitions, auto shows, and dynamic events such as Goodwood and Pebble Beach—experiences that sparked the idea behind the Salone dell'Auto format, which has now also evolved into the Milano Monza Motor Show.

guests.bio: Luca Bruschi is the director of AEVF, European Association of the Via Francigena Ways. As Director, Bruschi is at the forefront of the nomination of the Via Francigena as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In July, the preliminary dossier was officially submitted in Paris, focusing on the Italian section of the route from the Great St. Bernard Pass to Rome. The next stage of the candidacy will begin at the end of September 2025: this phase involves compiling the final dossier, identifying the cultural assets to be included on the UNESCO list, producing detailed cartography, and organizing participatory meetings with local communities along the route.The Via Francigena is certified Cultural Route of the Council of Europe. More than 3000 kilometers, from Canterbury to Rome and Santa Maria di Leuca, to walk step by step on mountain paths, mule tracks, rural and secondary roads, cypress-lined dirt roads or among majestic pines. Bruschi has personally completed the Via Francigena, the Camino de Santiago, and many other pilgrimage routes and cultural itineraries across Europe.

Deer had (almost) completely disappeared from Italy after World War II.
 Now the species is in a good state of conservation. The deer is the largest wild ruminant herbivore in Italy. In many areas, especially in parks and protected areas, numbers and densities are very high. This has a significant impact on vegetation, so much so that the deer is referred to as the engineer of ecosystems. Now, with the spontaneous return of the wolf to the Alps, we are entering a new phase of ecosystem balance. The arrival of the predator may change the numbers and behavior of prey, and this, in turn, may have an effect on vegetation. The study of trophic cascades in parks and its usefulness.

guests.bio: My name is Valerio Minato, born in Biella in 1981, and I discovered photography in 2012, almost by chance, as a passion that began during the final stages of my studies in Forestry and Environmental Sciences at the University of Turin. What started as a hobby soon grew into a true vocation: inspired by my love for Turin, the city that adopted me, I began capturing its panoramas and iconic views with increasing dedication and success. A self-taught photographer, I have developed a personal style that combines innovative shooting angles and daring perspectives, offering fresh and original interpretations of familiar landscapes. My academic background, along with a strong passion for geography and cartography, often guides me in the search for unique vantage points and striking visual alignments—for example, photographing Monviso and the Milan skyline from the Bergamo province. Over the years, my projects and images have gained recognition and have been featured in major online outlets and national newspapers, including *La Stampa, Repubblica,* and *Tuttosport*.

guests.bio: Luca Morino, born in Turin in 1962, is an Italian singer, composer, writer, and cultural promoter. He is the founder and lead singer of Mau Mau, a band that blends folk, African rhythms, and sonic contaminations. He has also released solo projects such as Mistic Turistic, Vox Creola, and, in 2024, DeWest. DeWest is a journey into the Far West — an oneiric, deconstructed territory ideally located in the Lower Piedmont region,  which corresponds, in a disorienting geography, to the Alta Langa area. The music of DeWest could be described, if such a genre existed, as voodoo folk: cinematic, expansive, yet also ritualistic, almost sacred, though within a secular vision. Beyond music, he writes, curates columns, and takes part in cultural initiatives in Piedmont and beyond.

Beyond novels, Strukul has written graphic novels (including a trilogy on Vlad the Impaler) and works as a screenwriter. guests.bio:
"Porta Palazzo - Storia orale e sensoriale del mercato più grande d’Europa" (Donzelli Ed.) Since 1835, Turin’s Porta Palazzo market has been a hub for observing the city’s social, cultural, and urban changes. A daily resource for working-class communities, it fosters transcultural encounters where diverse food practices and knowledge evolve. A destination for migrants from Piedmont, southern Italy, Africa, Asia, and Latin America, it embodies historical and diasporic layers, blending global and local dynamics. Through over 200 interviews with vendors, customers, and Turin’s diasporic communities, Gabriele Proglio crafts a narrative using food as a memory tool, capturing sensory recollections and emotions. In this liminal space, individual and collective stories intertwine, reflecting a city where past, present, and future meet at the market stalls.
Gabriele Proglio is an assoc. prof. of Contemporary History at the University of Gastronomic Sciences in Pollenzo. He has worked at the University of California, Berkeley, the European University Institute, Université El Manar in Tunis, and the universities of Coimbra, Ankara, and Grenoble. Among his recent publications in the field of oral history are The Horn of Africa Diasporas in Italy: An Oral History (Palgrave, 2020) and I fatti di Genova (Donzelli, 2021).

guests.bio: Iuri Moscardi is a PhD candidate in Comparative Literature (Italian Specialization) at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York. He studied Cesare Pavese during his years at Università degli Studi di Milano: his Bachelor degree thesis focused on the end of the American myth in The Moon and the Bonfires and his Master degree thesis, awarded with the Premio Pavese 2012, analyzed the typescript of the first Italian translation of Spoon River Anthology, proving the role of Pavese as editor of Fernanda Pivano’s translation. After having obtained his Master degree, he moved to the United States and in 2016 he received a Master of Arts in Italian from Indiana University, Bloomington. Since 2012, he has been involved in the digital social reading experiments of TwLetteratura and Betwyll, at the center of his dissertation research. He edited the collection of essays Cesare Pavese Mythographer, Translator, Modernist: A Collection of Studies 70 Years after His Death (2023) and the new, complete English translation of Pavese’s Mestiere di vivere (2025). He has also published articles and essays, in journals and volumes, in Italian and English, focused on Pavese and contemporary Italian literature. For Fondazione Cesare Pavese he is created "Dialoghi con Pavese", a bilingual column with interviews to Pavese's scholars around the world and the series of video interviews "Io vengo di là – Qualcosa di molto serio e prezioso" and "Un Pavese ci vuole". He conducted a research on the books donated by the Molina family to Fondazione Cesare Pavese, published on the academic journal Italica and presented during a symposium at New York University in 2023. As a freelance journalist, he writes about cultural and literary topics on La Lettura, Giornale di Brescia, Il Foglio, and il manifesto.

"Can I take a photo of your dog?" is the question Navid Tarazi uses to approach every human–animal pair. From that simple phrase was born @doggodaiily, the photographic project that has become a hugely popular page on Instagram and TikTok, where Navid tells the stories of the dogs he meets every day. From there also comes the book “Can I take a photo of your dog?”, published by Mondadori Electa, a volume that collects the portraits and stories of the many dogs and owners encountered by chance on the street. Navid Tarazi is an Iranian guy who moved to Italy in 2022. He studies Environmental Engineering at the Politecnico di Torino and has a passion for photography. In his home country, dogs are not considered pets, so while walking the streets of Italy, Navid is struck by the affectionate relationships he sees between four-legged friends and humans, and he wants to better understand the canine world.

guests.bio: My name is Valerio Minato, born in Biella in 1981, and I discovered photography in 2012, almost by chance, as a passion that began during the final stages of my studies in Forestry and Environmental Sciences at the University of Turin. What started as a hobby soon grew into a true vocation: inspired by my love for Turin, the city that adopted me, I began capturing its panoramas and iconic views with increasing dedication and success. A self-taught photographer, I have developed a personal style that combines innovative shooting angles and daring perspectives, offering fresh and original interpretations of familiar landscapes. My academic background, along with a strong passion for geography and cartography, often guides me in the search for unique vantage points and striking visual alignments—for example, photographing Monviso and the Milan skyline from the Bergamo province. Over the years, my projects and images have gained recognition and have been featured in major online outlets and national newspapers, including *La Stampa, Repubblica,* and *Tuttosport*.

Lucia Cimini is a historian and cultural commentator. She writes on cultural topics for Corriere della Sera and L’Espresso. Since 2023, she has been a regular contributor to the TV program Passato e Presente, broadcast on Rai 3 and Rai Storia. Finché tutto splende is her debut novel.
Balancing historical reality and imagination with remarkable finesse, Finché tutto splende traces the fascinating lives of the Necchi sisters over eighty years, through moments of joy, sorrow, and unexpected turns. From everyday life to the glamorous social scene of Milan in the 1920s and 1930s, from the dark years of war to the legacy left to the FAI, the novel offers an intimate portrait of a family and the villa that safeguarded their dreams, leaving a lasting mark on the city’s history.
With Lucia Cimini, we will also discuss the 80th anniversary of the Italian Republic.

guests.bio:
Gianduja it officially originated at the beginning of the 19th century (around 1804–1808) as a puppet created by the Turin puppeteers Giovanni Battista Sales and Gioachino Bellone. 
The name derives from the Piedmontese expression "Gioann dla doja" → "Giovanni of the tankard" (or "Giovanni of the jug"; doja or douja is the typical Piedmontese wine jug/boccale). It therefore represents a cheerful character, a lover of good wine, good-natured, a bit cunning, seemingly naive but full of common sense, generous, and fond of good company.

guests.bio:
Giuseppe Culicchia (Turin, 1965), writer, essayist and translator. Former bookseller, author of numerous successful novels, he is the director of the Fondazione Circolo dei Lettori (April 2025). 
The first edition of Francesissimo — a mirror and complementary project to Italissimo, which for ten years has brought Italian literature and culture to Paris — will take place in Turin from 30 January to 1 February 2026, bringing the French literature and culture festival to the city: meetings with French and francophone authors and author-esses, readings and film screenings, designed to foster dialogue between the cultural world across the Alps and the Italian public.
Francesissimo, conceived by the Fondazione Circolo dei Lettori and the Consulate General of France in Milan, and curated by Fabio Gambaro, will be held at the Circolo dei Lettori e delle Lettrici, Cinema Massimo, Alliance Française Torino, and the Biblioteca Civica Centrale.
The festival opens with Daniel Pennac. It closes with Boualem Sansal: his first public appearance following the pardon he received on 12 November last year from his country, Algeria, where he had been imprisoned since November 2024 for “undermining national unity”.

guests.bio:
Active in the delivery of major international events since 2011, Irene has built extensive experience in Ceremonies, working at senior level as a Cast and Volunteer Manager. In the early years of her career, she held Cast Manager roles across a number of global sporting events, leading the recruitment and management of volunteer performers and talent for Opening and Closing Ceremonies. Her experience includes UEFA EURO 2012, the Baku 2015 European Games, the Jakarta 2015 Asian Para Games, the Baku 2017 Islamic Solidarity Games, and the 5th Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games in Turkmenistan in 2017.
In 2018, she transitioned from Ceremonies into Volunteer Management, joining the UEFA EURO 2020 Volunteer Programme in Rome. Alongside this role, she continued to collaborate on football-related Ceremonies, including the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations in Gabon, the 2020 African Nations Championship, and the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations in Cameroon. In subsequent years, she also contributed to the delivery of several UEFA competitions, such as the 2019 UEFA European Under-21 Championship, the UEFA Nations League Finals, and the 2022 UEFA Women’s Champions League Final.
She later relocated abroad to work as Deputy Project Director, overseeing operations and delivery for the Islamic Arts Biennale at the Diriyah Biennale Foundation. She is currently involved in the organisation of the Milano Cortina 2026 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, having contributed from the outset to the planning and development of Team26, the official volunteer programme of Milano Cortina 2026.

Maurizio Gherardini is the 19th President in the history of Lega Basket Serie A.
He played, served as assistant coach, and was general manager for Libertas Forlì. He then moved to Benetton Treviso (General Manager starting in 1992). During his time in Treviso, the team won four Italian League titles (scudetti), one EuroLeague (Coppa d’Europa), one Saporta Cup, seven Italian Cups, and three Italian Supercups. While at Benetton, Gherardini was voted Best Executive of Lega Basket in 2006 and received the prestigious “Oscar del Basket - Pietro Reverberi” award in 2003. Gherardini was also a member of the FIBA Sports Commission from 1998 to 2000, and served on the EuroLeague board from 2001 to 2006 and from 2014 onward, additionally earning the ‘EuroLeague Executive of the Year’ award in 2017. In 2006, he moved to the NBA, where he served as Vice President and Assistant General Manager of the Toronto Raptors, becoming the first European executive to join an NBA club's front office. During this period, he also spent 7 years as Managing Director of the men's national team sector for the Canadian Basketball Federation and remains a permanent member of Canada Basketball's Council of Excellence. Later, in November 2013, he joined the Oklahoma City Thunder staff as senior advisor and head of international affairs.
From 2014 to 2025, he led the basketball operations at Fenerbahçe Istanbul, winning the EuroLeague in 2017 and 2025, six Turkish Super League titles (scudetti), six Turkish Cups, and three Turkish Presidential Cups (Supercoppe).

Andrea Bargnani (26 October 1985) is an Italian former professional basketball player. The 7-foot (2.13 m) power forward-center played for Benetton Treviso in the Italian LBA and the EuroLeague before being selected first overall in the 2006 NBA draft by the Toronto Raptors. He spent 10 seasons in the NBA, including with the New York Knicks and Brooklyn Nets, before ending his career with a stint in Spain during the 2016–17 season.  He was: the first European in history to be selected as the overall number one pick; the second non-American after the Chinese Yao Ming.

L’iniziativa si colloca all’interno del museo virtuale della scienza Unesco, piattaforma globale nata nell’ambito del decennio internazionale delle scienze per lo sviluppo sostenibile, con l’obiettivo di promuovere un accesso aperto, inclusivo e globale alla cultura scientifica. guests.bio: Massimiliano Lisa is the Director and co-founder of the Museo Leonardo3 in Milan, an interactive museum devoted to the genius of Leonardo da Vinci. Opened in 2013 in the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, the museum is known for reconstructing working machines directly from Leonardo’s original drawings. Under Lisa’s direction, researchers and engineers have recreated many of these designs, helping visitors understand how Leonardo imagined technology centuries ahead of its time. With a background in journalism, publishing and digital media, Lisa has spent many years combining technology and cultural heritage. Through the Leonardo3 research centre, he works on interpreting Leonardo’s manuscripts and transforming them into physical models and digital experiences. Among the museum’s most fascinating projects are the reconstructions of Leonardo’s mechanical clocks and timekeeping devices.

guests.bio: Daniela Tommasini is an Italian researcher and writer with a long-standing connection to Greenland and Arctic communities. Trained in political science and human geography, she has spent decades studying life in remote regions and the relationship between people, environment, and local development. Since her first journey to Greenland in the 1990s, she has regularly returned to the island, building close relationships with local communities. Her work combines academic research with personal storytelling about everyday life in the Arctic. Through her writings and public talks, she offers a unique perspective on cultures, landscapes, and the challenges of living in one of the most remote places on Earth. She is the author of In Groenlandia, a book that recounts her experiences and observations from years spent traveling across the island.

A very large community surrounds Ugolize, which in recent years has managed to win the affection of a wide audience—from Generation Z to the under-35s and even older generations. This is largely thanks to the ironic tone of their content, which is always able to spark awareness while simultaneously encouraging reflection on important social issues in our increasingly globalized societies.

Ugolize have also released their book *“Ugolize: Avventure fuori dagli schemi”* (*Ugolize: Adventures Off the Beaten Path*), a perfect read for getting a laugh even after a terrible day. It features an endless stream of witty one-liners, with the spotlight on original and entertaining cartoons starring the round-headed little characters that have made so many people laugh on social media.

The themes explored by Ugolize range from everyday life to contemporary challenges, with particular attention to common situations that intertwine irony and social reality. Among the main topics they address are generational differences, the paradoxes of the workplace, and current social issues such as climate change and technology—along with reflective and humorous insights that are always presented through a carefully tailored generational lens.

guests.bio:
By David Lawrence and Francesco Longo
Photographs that tell the story of the artist through the eyes of his brother Terry Burns.
Ninety photographs construct a narrative about David Bowie that begins with a private relationship and spans the artist’s entire public trajectory. David Bowie, My Brother is a project by writer David Lawrence, presented for the first time in Italy—after its exhibition in Paris—from April 17 to July 12 at Musa Art Gallery in Turin. 
The perspective is defined by the exhibition’s structure: the figure of Terry Burns, Bowie’s half-brother, becomes the lens through which images, texts, and materials are interpreted. Not a retrospective, but a journey that connects biographical episodes, cultural references, and the construction of artistic identity

Sean Albain was born in Glasgow in 1988. After a troubled youth, he left Scotland at fifteen and fell into heroin use in Ireland. His father’s death became a turning point: he returned to Glasgow, worked in bars, and studied theatre. At twenty, he set off for Africa with a guitar, traveling and performing across Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and South Africa. After a failed attempt to reach India, he moved to Southeast Asia in 2011, living on the streets through hardship and danger.
He later returned to Europe and settled in Milan, where he performed at the Colonne di San Lorenzo and began his music career. During the Covid period, he taught English online and studied psychology and philosophy. He now lives in Dovera (Lombardy), where he teaches and writes. His debut album, You’ll Be Fine, reflects his nomadic and challenging life journey.

Benjamin Pritchard is a British para-rower. He won the gold medal in the men’s PR1 single sculls at the 2024 Summer Paralympics and also claimed gold at the 2025 European Rowing Championships, setting a world record.

A former cyclist and triathlete, Benjamin’s journey took an unexpected turn when he became paralysed from the waist down following a cycling crash in September 2016. During his rehabilitation at Stoke Mandeville Hospital, he discovered indoor rowing, quickly catching the attention of British Rowing staff. He joined the para development squad in 2017 and has never looked back.

His natural talent and dedication propelled him onto the international stage, making his GB Rowing Team debut in the PR1 men’s single sculls at the 2019 World Championships. After finishing fifth at the delayed Tokyo Paralympic Games—where he set a Paralympic record—he continued his rise, securing two World Championship podium finishes. In 2024, he became Paralympic Champion in Paris, setting another Paralympic record in the process.

Beyond his achievements on the water, Benjamin is a passionate advocate for athletes, representing their voices on both the World Rowing and British Paralympic Association Athletes’ Commissions. He is also gaining experience in two of his passions—coffee and BBC local radio. He is married to Meg and is a proud father to Efa.

Benjamin Pritchard is a British para-rower. He won the gold medal in the men’s PR1 single sculls at the 2024 Summer Paralympics and also claimed gold at the 2025 European Rowing Championships, setting a world record.

A former cyclist and triathlete, Benjamin’s journey took an unexpected turn when he became paralysed from the waist down following a cycling crash in September 2016. During his rehabilitation at Stoke Mandeville Hospital, he discovered indoor rowing, quickly catching the attention of British Rowing staff. He joined the para development squad in 2017 and has never looked back.

His natural talent and dedication propelled him onto the international stage, making his GB Rowing Team debut in the PR1 men’s single sculls at the 2019 World Championships. After finishing fifth at the delayed Tokyo Paralympic Games—where he set a Paralympic record—he continued his rise, securing two World Championship podium finishes. In 2024, he became Paralympic Champion in Paris, setting another Paralympic record in the process.

Beyond his achievements on the water, Benjamin is a passionate advocate for athletes, representing their voices on both the World Rowing and British Paralympic Association Athletes’ Commissions. He is also gaining experience in two of his passions—coffee and BBC local radio. He is married to Meg and is a proud father to Efa.

A very large community surrounds Ugolize, which in recent years has managed to win the affection of a wide audience—from Generation Z to the under-35s and even older generations. This is largely thanks to the ironic tone of their content, which is always able to spark awareness while simultaneously encouraging reflection on important social issues in our increasingly globalized societies.

The themes explored by Ugolize range from everyday life to contemporary challenges, with particular attention to common situations that intertwine irony and social reality. He played, served as assistant coach, and was general manager for Libertas Forlì. He then moved to Benetton Treviso (General Manager starting in 1992). Gherardini was also a member of the FIBA Sports Commission from 1998 to 2000, and served on the EuroLeague board from 2001 to 2006 and from 2014 onward, additionally earning the ‘EuroLeague Executive of the Year’ award in 2017. In 2006, he moved to the NBA, where he served as Vice President and Assistant General Manager of the Toronto Raptors, becoming the first European executive to join an NBA club's front office. During this period, he also spent 7 years as Managing Director of the men's national team sector for the Canadian Basketball Federation and remains a permanent member of Canada Basketball's Council of Excellence. Later, in November 2013, he joined the Oklahoma City Thunder staff as senior advisor and head of international affairs.
From 2014 to 2025, he led the basketball operations at Fenerbahçe Istanbul, winning the EuroLeague in 2017 and 2025, six Turkish Super League titles (scudetti), six Turkish Cups, and three Turkish Presidential Cups (Supercoppe).

A self-taught photographer, I have developed a personal style that combines innovative shooting angles and daring perspectives, offering fresh and original interpretations of familiar landscapes. My academic background, along with a strong passion for geography and cartography, often guides me in the search for unique vantage points and striking visual alignments—for example, photographing Monviso and the Milan skyline from the Bergamo province. Deer had (almost) completely disappeared from Italy after World War II.
 Now the species is in a good state of conservation. The deer is the largest wild ruminant herbivore in Italy. In many areas, especially in parks and protected areas, numbers and densities are very high. This has a significant impact on vegetation, so much so that the deer is referred to as the engineer of ecosystems. Now, with the spontaneous return of the wolf to the Alps, we are entering a new phase of ecosystem balance. The arrival of the predator may change the numbers and behavior of prey, and this, in turn, may have an effect on vegetation. The study of trophic cascades in parks and its usefulness.

Luca Bruschi is the director of AEVF, European Association of the Via Francigena Ways. As Director, Bruschi is at the forefront of the nomination of the Via Francigena as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In July, the preliminary dossier was officially submitted in Paris, focusing on the Italian section of the route from the Great St. Bernard Pass to Rome. The next stage of the candidacy will begin at the end of September 2025: this phase involves compiling the final dossier, identifying the cultural assets to be included on the UNESCO list, producing detailed cartography, and organizing participatory meetings with local communities along the route.The Via Francigena is certified Cultural Route of the Council of Europe. More than 3000 kilometers, from Canterbury to Rome and Santa Maria di Leuca, to walk step by step on mountain paths, mule tracks, rural and secondary roads, cypress-lined dirt roads or among majestic pines. Bruschi has personally completed the Via Francigena, the Camino de Santiago, and many other pilgrimage routes and cultural itineraries across Europe.

SP has been translating Anglo-American literature for 25 years, mainly for the publishers Adelphi, Einaudi & Mondadori. She has translated, among others, Jonathan Franzen (of whom she is the Italian “voice”), Colson Whitehead, Don DeLillo, Isaac B. Singer, Cormac McCarthy, Zadie Smith, Shirley Jackson, and Junot Díaz. For Mondadori she has retranslated Ernest Hemingway’s The Old Man and the Sea and A Farewell to Arms, and she is set to retranslate For Whom the Bell Tolls. In 2019 she received the Classifica di Qualità award from la Lettura - Il Corriere della Sera for he translation of Denis Johnson’s The Largesse of the Sea Maiden, and in 2024 the Pavese Lifetime Achievement Award. She is the author of the short story collection I jeans di Bruce Springsteen e altri sogni americani (Giunti, 2016) and of Fra le righe. Il piacere di tradurre (Laterza, 2024). She lives on lake Maggiore.

Fabio Testi is the star who turned his good looks from a supposed “flaw” into a ticket to cinematic legend. Born in Peschiera del Garda, he started out as a stuntman — falling off horses, crashing motorbikes, and even hanging in midair for two weeks on the set of Barbarella. It was Vittorio De Sica who catapulted him to fame with the Oscar-winning The Garden of the Finzi-Continis in 1970. From there came a career packed with auteur films and popular hits (Addio fratello crudele, L’important c’est d’aimer with Romy Schneider, Camorra by Pasquale Squitieri), over a hundred screen and stage credits, and a love life straight out of the tabloids — Ursula Andress, Anita Ekberg, Charlotte Rampling, Edwige Fenech… Today, well into his eighties, Testi still keeps us guessing: he grows truffles by Lake Garda, tours with a poetry-and-music show, and pops up in international cinema — most recently in Reflet dans un diamant mort, which premiered at the Berlinale. Always elegant, always magnetic, he’s living proof that yes, there really are a few beautiful men who are also smart.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Professor SERGIO STEFANNI: Born in Desenzano del Garda (Italy) on 29/12/1967, after a Master Degree in marine studies at University of Genoa and a PhD at the School of Biological Science at the University of Bristol, he has been a researcher at Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn in Naples (Italy) since 2016. His research interests are molecular ecology, population genetics and phylogeny of marine organisms. He study mainly fish and sharks, from coastal to the deep-sea, but he's been a guest of Paparazzi helping our understanding of marine alien species in our seas like the lionfish and the silver-cheeked toadfish. ANDREA LEVY: Andrea Levy was born in Ancona on July 7, 1971. He specialized in international marketing and communication at the University of Nevada. His passion for cars has been with him since childhood. He grew up in Moncalieri, near Turin, where he saw prototypes and cars from legendary coachbuilders and manufacturers—Pininfarina, Giugiaro, Italdesign, and Fiat—come to life and hit the roads. Today, he is a successful entrepreneur in communication and events, a devoted collector of sports cars and supercars, and a true motorsport enthusiast. He races with Ferrari Club Italia and competes in Time Attack with Ferrari, Radical, and Dallara. Always on the move, he follows racing competitions, auto shows, and dynamic events such as Goodwood and Pebble Beach—experiences that sparked the idea behind the Salone dell'Auto format, which has now also evolved into the Milano Monza Motor Show.
